This enzyme catalyzes cleavage of the benzene ring [Kukor96]. A plasmid containing a DNA fragment from the Ralstonia pickettii (Pseudomonas pickettii) chromosome encoding enzymes of the catechol meta cleavage pathway allowed a Pseudomonas aeruginosa mutant to grow on toluene, or related compounds, as a sole carbon source. Catechol 2,3-dioxygenase activity was assayed in crude extracts. It was shown that 4-methylcatechol is an alternative substrate for the enzyme [Kukor91].

Although 4-methylcatechol is a suicide inhibitor of the enzyme, it has been shown that a bacterial repair system regenerates Fe(II) from Fe(III) in the enzyme, using a [2Fe-2S] ferredoxin [Hugo00], and in [Okuta04].
